user_prompt: What is the effect of multifaceted implementation interventions (for example education, audit and feedback, local champions, protocols or clinical pathways, with or without changes to how care is delivered), compared with no implementation intervention or usual practice, on adherence to evidence-based recommendations in the care of people with acute stroke during the hospital admission?  Effect measure: pool as a risk ratio (RR) of adherence, intervention divided by control, using a random-effects model on the log risk ratio. RR > 1 means higher adherence with the intervention.  Outcome: the proportion of patients (or eligible patients) who received the recommended process of care, extracted as the number adherent (events) out of the number in each arm (total), at the end of the intervention period. - Use the trial's primary adherence or quality-of-care process measure (for example the proportion of eligible patients given thrombolysis, or the proportion receiving a defined care protocol). Do not use patient outcomes such as death, disability or length of stay. - If a trial reports several process measures, use the primary one and report which was used. - Use the numbers of patients, not hospitals or clusters, as events and totals, from the follow-up period after the intervention started (not baseline). If a trial reports a before-and-after comparison, use the post-intervention period only. - Cluster-randomised trials: if the paper reports a cluster-adjusted risk ratio or odds ratio with a confidence interval, use that (convert the interval to a standard error of the log RR; convert an odds ratio to a risk ratio only if the baseline risk is given). Otherwise adjust the standard error by the design effect, 1 + (average cluster size − 1) × ICC, with the ICC reported by the trial or, if none is reported, state an assumed ICC of 0.05. - Control: no intervention, usual care or practice as normal. Exclude trials whose control group receives another implementation strategy. - Multi-arm trials: include only the multifaceted-intervention arm and the control arm; combine several intervention arms into one. - Include only randomised (including cluster-randomised) trials in acute stroke settings. Exclude single-component interventions, studies in other conditions, and uncontrolled before-and-after studies.  Do not pool patient clinical outcomes, costs, staff knowledge or satisfaction, or adherence measured after the hospital admission.
